youtube_description:
Here's exactly what you should be buying for your health, whether you're dead broke, middle class, or making over $10,000 a month. Money does you no good if you're dead or if you're sick, so no matter how little you have right now, you need to be spending more on your health.

See what you'd look like with a six-pack, free:
https://absbyai.com/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=longform&utm_content=ro20c-what-to-buy

If you're dead broke:
1. A basic home workout setup for under $100: yoga mat, push-up handles, light dumbbells, a kettlebell, an ab wheel and a jump rope
2. Basic healthy food: chicken, a little rice and cruciferous vegetables from Costco

If you're middle class:
1. The best protein money can buy (wild-caught salmon, filet mignon)
2. A better mattress
3. A membership at the gym with the best people, not the best equipment
4. A sleep tracker
5. GLP-1 medication
6. TRT
7. Three cheap supplements: fish oil, vitamin D and magnesium

If you're making over $10,000 a month:
1. A home gym
2. A meal prep service or a personal chef
3. A maid and a laundry service
4. A human personal trainer and nutritionist

This is part 3 of 3 in my Invest In Your Health series. Part 1, why you should invest more in your health, and part 2, what to cut to afford getting in shape, came out the last two Sundays (links added once they're live).
